discovery: Quantum simulation of many-body physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: J. Ignacio Cirac
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, Garching, Germany

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum many-body physics
motivation: Cirac and Zoller (with Jaksch and co-workers, 1998) showed that ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise the Bose-Hubbard model with fully tunable parameters, turning laser light into a programmable crystal for quantum matter. Bloch's 2002 observation of the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator transition confirmed this vision and launched quantum simulation as an experimental science. Bloch then introduced single-site-resolved quantum gas microscopy, observing magnetic correlations, many-body localisation and out-of-equilibrium dynamics atom by atom. Together with Cirac and Zoller's theoretical framework for engineering Hamiltonians, entanglement and quantum control, this programme answered Feynman's call to simulate quantum systems with quantum systems. Its tools now underpin the world's most precise optical lattice clocks, entanglement-enhanced metrology, ultracold molecule and Rydberg-array platforms, and analog quantum simulators worldwide. Few developments have so profoundly opened a new, controllable window onto strongly correlated quantum matter.
